newsitem.title: USA: Marker says snowboard oversupply to hurt DNR unit.
newsitem.headline: Marker says snowboard oversupply to hurt DNR unit.

text.p: Marker International said Wednesday the current oversupply of production worldwide would hurt its new 80-percent owned subsidiary, DNR Sportsystem Ltd.
Hank Tauber, president and chief executive officer of the company, said in a statement the the situation "will negatively impact sales and profitability of DNR."
He said it will also reduce the planned production volume of Marker's snowboard manufacturing facility in Salt Lake City in fiscal 1998.
Tauber noted that, after several years of consistent earnings, Marker anticipates that its current fiscal year ending March 31, 1998, will be a "transitional year."
But the company remains optimistic about performance of its core ski alpine ski binding and MArker Ltd clothing businesses, he said.

Tauber made the comment as Marker announced net earnings for its fiscal 1997 fourth quarter ending March 31 of $0.02 a share, on net income of $260,000 for the year-ago quarter. The results compare with per share earnings of $0.05 on net income of $392,000 a year ago.
It said net earnings per share for the 1997 fiscal year rose to $0.45 on net sales of $126.4 million, from $0.40 on net sales of $87.9 million a year ago.
